docs.title: A context playbook, evolved¶
docs.text:
The EvoSkill sibling evolves prose an agent reads whole. This one evolves a playbook: canonical JSON whose entries carry stable logical identities, so a single entry can be amended or retired without losing its history -- and without rewriting the other entries.

Same boundary as the sibling, same deterministic fixture agent, no credential. The example README is the canonical explanation.

The whole lifecycle is one call, so that is what comes first. Everything after it inspects the result.

docs.title: Why identity is the whole point¶
docs.text: A playbook is one meta.Text holding canonical JSON -- sorted keys, no spare whitespace -- so two equal playbooks have byte-identical digests. Each entry keeps its identity across an amendment, and retiring one keeps it in the record instead of deleting it.

docs.title: Three splits, two tagging policies¶
docs.text:
The same two policies appear in every split, over differently worded disclosures. That is deliberate: an entry earns its keep by carrying one filer's policy to a note nobody has read yet, so the private and held-out rollouts must not be the development ones renamed.

Development failures are the only thing a proposer is allowed to learn from, and only the ones that finished and were wrong -- a rollout that faulted is not evidence, so it buys no feedback. The held-out split runs once, after selection.

docs.title: What that one call did¶
docs.text:
Development, search, consolidation, held out -- in the one order they are valid in. study_playbook owns that order, so a caller cannot skip the consolidation re-score or run held-out before selection, and nothing below re-drives a phase: it all reads off the study from the first cell.

The seed is a tagging manual that is already wrong in two different ways: it names the standard element where this filer uses its own extension, and it carries a presentation rule nothing in the evidence supports. So the first proposal has to curate -- amend the rescuable entry, retire the unsupported one -- before the second can grow the playbook.

The result also carries the curator's declaration. A local component is named by module and qualname, so two closures from one factory compare equal; the curator therefore declares a digest over the published lesson manifest, and two runs given different lessons cannot record the same proposer and the same run id while producing different playbooks.

docs.title: Four ways to be unrankable¶
docs.text: A low score means the playbook was wrong. None of these do, so none of them is allowed to be a low score. Two are about the candidate:

docs.title: A split that did not finish has no score¶
docs.text: One success beside one timeout is not 1.0. Averaging whatever finished would be a claim about the playbook that the evidence does not support, so a partial split refuses to summarise itself -- and the study names the phase and the kind instead.

docs.title: Change and predict¶
docs.text:
This runs in a cell too. revise takes the published lessons and nothing else, so you can hand it your own and watch curation decide -- no repository file to edit, no kernel to restart.

Give it a lesson that contradicts an entry the seed already states, and predict which of three things happens before you run it: does the mechanism amend that entry, retire it, or append a second one that disagrees?

from ace_curation import revise
from ace_rollouts import Lesson

contradiction = Lesson(
    identity="interest-element", section="debt", marker="nwi:InterestPaidGross",
    content="Cash interest is tagged nwi:InterestPaidGross, before capitalization.",
)
result = revise((contradiction,))(codec.encode(SEED_PLAYBOOK), None)
[(item.identity, item.status) for item in codec.decode(result.candidate).items]

Which of the three would you want? And if the proposal is refused instead, read result.failure -- a refused transition is an outcome here, not a crash.

The EvoSkill sibling is in evoskill.ipynb.

Neither notebook reproduces its paper's system, benchmarks, transfer results, or reported gains. They demonstrate a mechanism.

docs.title: Skill documents, evolved¶
docs.text:
Can an outer run improve what an agent is told -- a set of skills/<name>.md documents -- while the budget, the episode list, and the scoring all stay outside what a candidate can touch?

Every cell below imports the committed example's own modules and drives its own functions through the deterministic fixture agent the script injects, so nothing here needs a credential, a network, or a dollar. The example README is the canonical explanation; this is a place to poke at it.

docs.title: Run the search¶
docs.text:
Three evaluations: the empty seed, then two proposals that each add one whole skill document. There is one skill per episode, so a candidate holding neither scores 0.0, one scores 0.5, and both score 1.0.

The wrapper below remembers, which is what a live SDK client is, and records every task each session was shown. Both numbers matter and they say different things. Six sessions is the arithmetic: one per episode, not one per candidate, which is why the declared ceiling counts proposals. One task per session is the property: both notes are tagged by a policy that appears in no workspace, so a session spanning them would let the second answer from the first -- and that reads exactly like the skill set carrying the knowledge.

InnerAgent is how the wrapper arrives: the factory bound to what it declares itself to be. A model id alone would not do, and the next section is why.

docs.title: The losers are still there¶
docs.text: run.trials() keeps every candidate in order, so the climb is inspectable rather than summarised. The intermediate 0.5 is what makes the run evidence about the skill text: the fixture agent never changes, so nothing else could have moved the score.

docs.title: Why a model id is not an agent¶
docs.text:
The skill set is the only thing a proposal changes. The budget, the episode list, and the evaluator live in the declaration above it -- and the evaluator declares what it was configured with, because the agent lives inside its closure where a run-local reference cannot see it.

Below, two agents declare the same model, the same revision, and the same configuration, and differ only in the wrapper behind them. That is the point of the cell: every string a caller can claim is held fixed, so the separation has to come from the factory itself. Wrapper revision, SDK version, tool permissions and turn limits are all things a model id cannot see -- but a caller who declares them identically for two different implementations still gets two versions, because the factory's own code is hashed too.

The cell prints both halves: that the declared fields are equal, and that the verified implementation digest is not.

docs.title: A failure is not a low score¶
docs.text: If the wrapper cannot produce a candidate at all, there is nothing to rank. The suite reports a typed failure carrying no metric, so it can never out-rank a skill set that merely scored badly -- and the fault each episode recorded is named rather than flattened into a zero.

docs.title: Change and predict¶
docs.text:
This runs in a cell. No repository file to edit, no kernel to restart -- the wrapper is yours, and InnerAgent is how you hand it over.

Write one that hears the interest policy and is deaf to the lease one, then predict all three trial scores before running it:

def half_deaf(instructions):
    inner = FIXTURE_AGENT.build(instructions)

    def propose(tree, context):
        return inner(tree, context) if "note_05_interest.tag" in tree else tree

    return propose


half = evolve_skills(
    InnerAgent(build=half_deaf, model="half-deaf-v1", revision="half-deaf-v1")
)
[trial.metrics["solved"] for trial in half.trials()]

Then the harder question: when the score stops moving, did the search get worse, or did the two episodes stop disagreeing about what a skill has to say?

docs.title: Documentation audit and editorial conventions
docs.text: The documentation entrance follows one evaluated prompt-improvement story: meeting notes become structured action items. The implementation uses shipped APIs through M10. This refresh adds examples and explanations, not framework capabilities. M11 remains Design—not shipped.

docs.title: Ownership and navigation
docs.text:
Section Reader's question Content owner Home Why use this? README, homepage, and first-run lesson Learn How does the loop work? Meeting-notes scripts and captured outputs Recipes How does this apply to my problem? Each maintained example implementation How-to How do I perform this specific task? Task-oriented guides under the programming model Concepts Why does it work this way? Explanations linked to canonical architecture Reference What does this API accept and return? Source signatures and programming model Project What exists and how do I contribute? Status, architecture, research, and roadmap

The learning order is first run, define better, inspect, choose search, use feedback, keep the run, and apply the loop elsewhere. Existing lesson filenames are preserved; navigation and next links determine order. Source repair is a recipe. Checklists, integer examples, and historical evidence notebooks remain available as supplements rather than competing introductions.

The programming model owns the shipped API; architecture owns domain semantics. Milestones and the implementation plan retain their existing authority. Design proposals remain subordinate. Example fixtures do not establish live-model performance, research replication, or generalization.

docs.title: Lesson conventions
docs.text:
A lesson follows a practical question, executable code, captured output, explanation, and one focused exercise. Introduce seed, proposer, evaluator, trials, and search as needed. Explain the returned Run and its relevant views in terms of the question being answered. Show actual response evidence, not only scores. Prefer readable fields to raw object dumps.

The prompt is the versioned artifact; response text is evidence for its measurement. The seed is evaluated separately from successor attempts. A revision can regress. Retain rejected attempts and show why best() can return a prompt other than the final proposal.

The first run uses handwritten response fixtures with visible replacement points. Feedback is explicitly introduced through Experiment and bounded context; it is not automatically sent by improve(). Final-check inputs stay outside selection and rewriting. Wrappers own SDK configuration and calls; known model usage accompanies successful and failed outcomes.

Failed measurements have no score. A completed but incorrect task response can have a low score. Durable storage permits later inspection; verified registered components are additionally required for resume. Selection is never deployment.

docs.title: Evidence and compatibility
docs.text:
Canonical scripts supply site snippets. README code and displayed output use the existing captured-output validation. Fixtures are labeled next to output; no live-looking transcript is substituted for an unexecuted SDK call.

Keep old routes and required fragment anchors reachable. The historical route baseline must not be weakened to accommodate a reorganization. Notebook mirrors stay byte-identical, and site builds never execute saved notebooks. No new notebook or theme redesign is part of this refresh.

Recipes identify editable content, independent grading, selection data, separate final checks when present, replacement points, and evidence limitations. The original support-ticket recipe remains an additional source-tree example; the meeting-notes integration uses direct model calls.

docs.title: Review record
docs.text:
The six implementation stages cover the example, companions, learning-path switch, SDK guidance, concepts/recipes, and navigation review. Each stage's PR records its focused verification. Integration requires the full test suite, fresh captured outputs, compilation, strict site build, and rendered link checks.

Desktop and mobile inspection must cover navigation, code blocks, JSON, and output readability. A human newcomer walkthrough remains a reviewer task: start at README, run the example, find a failed response, change the attempt bound, and explain what changed. Automated execution and agent visual inspection do not constitute human usability validation.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
The local author experience through Milestone 10 is shipped, and Milestones 1–8 are complete, as are Milestones 9, 9.5, and 10. Advanced search is shipped: Specialists and TreeSearch shipped through M9.5.3, and the unified five-policy comparison shipped in M9.5.4. Harness live validation closed on retained historical evidence; no live harness code beyond M8.5 merged to main. Distributed workers, federation, and the post-M10 notebook/browser presentation follow-up remain Design—not shipped.

The programming model owns the public API contract; the roadmap owns milestone status and scope.

docs.title: Measured local-author design target
docs.text: The M10.0 design scorecard measures a runnable shipped full-protocol search at 15 scaffolding lines and the statically counted proposed functional syntax at 1: a 93% reduction. The historical labels and counts remain unchanged; the M10.3 after-side now executes in deterministic unnumbered local fixtures. This measures authoring friction, not optimization quality or runtime performance.

docs.title: Shipped API reference
docs.text:
Every entry on this page is generated from the installed meta_evolve package. The four tiers organize the root imports without changing or hiding them.

The namespaced Specialists and TreeSearch presets (meta_evolve.policies.Specialists, meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch) are documented in the programming model and search guide; neither is a root export.

The optional Git history presentation is deliberately namespaced: GitHistoryView (meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView) is constructed from meta_evolve.adapters, and callback-only WorkspaceSession (meta_evolve.ports.WorkspaceSession) is exposed from meta_evolve.ports. Neither expands the root surface.

Read component composition for how these pieces fit together.

docs.title: Presentation records
docs.text: Only ArtifactPresentation and ArtifactDiff are root-exported records. Their minimal immutable supporting records live in meta_evolve.presentation: PresentationSection groups labelled PresentationField values and PresentationDocument text; each document has an optional path and explicit truncation state. FileDiff carries its path, added/removed/modified/unchanged status, typed DiffLine values with optional old/new line numbers, and an optional refusal or truncation notice. These records contain inert data only, not HTML, SVG, URLs, or trusted markup.

docs.title: Optional local browser
docs.text: The browser adds no root exports beyond the dependency-free presentation contract above. Install meta-evolve[browser] (or use uv sync --extra browser) and start meta-evolve ui --storage PATH. Its server-rendered routes are documented in the local browser guide.

docs.title: Generated entries
docs.text: The root package keeps the simple callable path small: define a task, bound it with a budget, and state what to maximize or minimize. The full durable vocabulary for policy authors and kernel code lives in meta_evolve.domain, the read-only graph query surface used by context policies is root-exported, and canonical serialization lives in meta_evolve.serialization.

docs.title: ArtifactView dataclass
docs.text:
One artifact occurrence with decoded and inert payload projections.

value retains the established author-facing decoded object. Safe presentation consumes only the private frozen payload captured beside it. The payload is deliberately absent from repr and equality so adding it does not change the existing public view semantics.

docs.text: Push records from accessible ancestors in graph and commit order.

docs.title: BestOfK dataclass
docs.text:
Sample k successors from the incumbent, then reselect it.

Any positive k is accepted. A k at or above max_trials simply means the run never completes a cohort, so the parent stays the seed for every trial — the same star BestOfN produces.

docs.title: bind(proposer, budget)
docs.text: Authorize one proposer and derive the unit trial allocation.

docs.title: BestOfN dataclass
docs.text:
Expand the seed independently for at most max_trials successor attempts.

Every proposal starts from the same seed. Explicitly enabled experience can still communicate prior observations between attempts. The seed can remain the winner; a successor need not improve it.

docs.title: CapabilityError
docs.text:
Bases: RunError

A run's declared or requested execution profile is not honored.

Raised for unverifiable component implementations (lambdas, closures, functools.partial, decorated wrappers, or callables with no resolvable module source), unregistered (role, name, version) lookups, and durable-local configuration that lacks a registry, durable storage, or a registered evaluator/proposer/policy. Also raised when storage is asked for an optional capability its components do not declare, such as enumerating runs through a non-RunIndex event store.

docs.title: ContextPolicy
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Select the exact bounded context bundle pushed to one proposer call.

Only records committed strictly before the candidate trial's logical step are eligible; context facts themselves are never eligible. The kernel rejects a bundle that selects anything else or exceeds the declared bounds.

docs.title: CommandEvaluator dataclass
docs.text:
Measure source in a fresh workspace using a fixed command.

Exit 0 reports passing_score; exit 1 reports failing_score. Other exits and process failures remain typed failures without rankable scores. Process results and environment identity are retained as evidence. The default development subprocess provider is not hostile-code isolation.

A bounded read capability supplied to successor proposers.

History queries and exact source listing, reads, and diffs observe only authorized prior occurrences. Operations are recorded and charged against the grant. Denied access and exhausted bounds raise typed exceptions; reading a record grants no authority to change it.

docs.title: EvaluationResult dataclass
docs.text:
Independent measurements or a typed failure, plus evidence and usage.

Successful metrics must cover the task objectives. A failed measurement has no rankable metrics. Return this explicitly to attach evidence, uncertainty, tokens, monetary spend, or elapsed usage; plain evaluators may return a scalar or metric mapping when no extra observations are needed.

docs.title: Experiment dataclass
docs.text:
An immutable evaluated-search declaration.

Execution starts only when passed to run or Session.start. Storage, mode, and a narrowing budget are execution overlays.

Equality is ordinary dataclass equality over these eight fields. In particular, no structural equality is promised for live proposer or registry objects.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default task Task

Evaluation contract, artifact type, objectives, and optional budget ceiling.

required seed object

required proposer ProposerLike

required search SearchProgram | None

Search policy; None means Greedy(max_trials=20) at execution time.

None context ContextPolicy | None

Optional policy-pushed experience selector.

None experience ExperienceAccess | None

Optional bounded agent-pulled experience access.

None random_seed int

Integer seed for recorded deterministic search choices; defaults to 0.

0 registry Registry | None

docs.title: usage()
docs.text:
Everything this run consumed, including work that failed to rank.

Use this rather than summary().usage whenever a caller is accumulating -- a roll-up over inner runs, or any total that must survive a bad episode. summary() raises NoSuccessfulEvaluation when a run scored nothing, which unwinds the caller and discards the resources already accumulated from earlier episodes as well as this one's. This reports the same figure as inspect().overview.task_usage and never raises for that reason.

A run that does not exist raises RunNotFound, as inspect() does. That is the point of require_existing: without it the unbootstrapped projection leaks a bare SearchNotStarted, and this accessor promises the same answers and the same errors as the aggregate it stands in for.

docs.title: Storage dataclass
docs.text:
Paired artifact and event storage, plus one all-or-none commit.

is_durable and is_read_only are independent capabilities. Durability says committed facts live on durable media; read-only says this handle has no commit authority. A writable durable handle therefore reports True, False while :meth:read_only reports True, True.

docs.title: durable(path) classmethod
docs.text: Wire durable storage into path (created if missing): one SQLite connection (events + artifact occurrence rows) shared with a content-addressed filesystem blob store under path/artifacts.

docs.title: read_only(path) classmethod
docs.text:
Open an existing durable directory with inspection authority only.

The directory and current schema must already exist. This path never creates, stamps, migrates, or otherwise repairs durable state.

docs.title: compose(artifacts, events, *, commit_strategy, close=None) classmethod
docs.text:
Compose independently implemented stores behind one atomic commit.

The strategy declares whether its commit survives process restart; callers cannot separately forge is_durable. Composed storage is always writable: Storage cannot verify that third-party stores genuinely refuse writes, so read-only inspection handles come only from :meth:read_only, which pairs the declaration with stores built to fail closed.

docs.title: commit(run_id, expected_version, *, events, occurrences)
docs.text:
Commit events and occurrences as one all-or-none unit.

EventStreamConflict on a stale expected_version propagates unchanged, and nothing is written. See unit_of_work.py for the per-backend guarantee (durable: one SQLite transaction; in-memory: a locked copy-on-write swap; hand-built pair: local-only fallback).

docs.title: runs()
docs.text:
Every run this storage holds events for, sorted by id.

Identities, not Run objects: opening a run validates and replays its whole stream, and detail is already Run.summary()'s job. A listing exists so those queries stay reachable once the ids have scrolled out of a terminal, so it returns exactly what reopening one needs. The order is lexicographic by id and identical across backends; run ids are content-derived, so it is not chronological.

Enumeration is an optional store capability (ports.RunIndex), declared by implementing it. A paired event store that does not is refused explicitly here — never reported as an empty store, which would be a silent capability downgrade.

docs.title: Usage dataclass

docs.title: without_counts property
docs.text:
The measured resources alone, with the kernel-minted counts dropped.

tokens, spend_micros and wall_seconds are measured -- a component reports what it consumed or was billed. trials and evaluations are minted by the coordinator, which is the only thing entitled to say how much work happened, so a component reporting them is invalid and a nested run's own counts belong to that run.

This is the projection every roll-up needs: total += inner.without_counts carries the money and tokens up while leaving the counts inside. It lives on the type that owns the fields so adding a dimension does not mean finding every caller that happened to enumerate them.

docs.title: Compose an improvement loop
docs.text:
Start with a seed, a proposer, and an evaluator. Add a search policy when you need to choose what to try next. This page explains how the components fit; the programming model owns the public contract, the architecture owns semantics, and the generated API owns exact signatures.

Component Receives Produces Authority Proposer Selected parent value; optional ProposerContext Candidate or ProposalResult Proposed content only Evaluator Candidate value Scalar, metric mapping, EvaluationResult, or failure Independent measurement Search Retained search state Parent choice, admission, stopping What to try next within bounds Context policy Authorized prior history Pushed ContextBundle What records to show a proposer Experience reader A bounded query from a proposer Audited prior records or source Read access within its grant

docs.title: Replace a proposer or evaluator
docs.text:
The prompt example uses two plain functions. An SDK wrapper uses the same boundary: it owns its client and session, then returns candidate content. Return ProposalResult to report provider usage, evidence, or a hypothesis. Return EvaluationResult when measurements need supporting evidence or uncertainty. Failures live in meta_evolve.domain and remain unrankable; they are never converted into zero scores.

For files, PatchProposer applies exact patches and CommandEvaluator runs independent checks. For new domains or advanced search, use the extension contracts and conformance suites. No provider or domain branch is needed in the execution engine.

docs.title: Separate push from pull
docs.text: Experiment(context=AncestorsOnly(...)) selects bounded records before a proposal. Experiment(experience=PullAccess(...)) gives the proposer an audited reader. They can be enabled separately or together; PullAccess is not a context policy. ProposerContext exposes the selected bundle, optional reader, randomness, objectives, step, and any adapter-provided workspace. Source access follows the same bounded read grant.

docs.title: Separate execution from results
docs.text:
Experiment declares the loop. run executes it; Session lets you pace the same execution. A Run reads retained facts. best().value gives the winner; inspect() and usage() also work when measurements failed. Persistent history is useful without resume capability; durable-local reconstruction adds the explicit component declarations needed to continue unfinished work.

Search selection never approves deployment. Keep evaluator authority, budgets, and final acceptance outside candidate content.

docs.title: Advanced experience provenance
docs.text:
This reference follows the outcome-first experience lesson.

Pushed and pulled observations enter one ordered ledger. Each entry records the run, occurrence kind and ID, logical step, event sequence, operation, result, and exact usage. A proposal's optional derived_from tuple must be an ordered subsequence of references that this proposer actually observed.

Validation rejects a reference that is missing, duplicated contrary to its ledger position, out of scope, from the future, content-inconsistent, or ordered differently from observation. Rejection is typed invalid output and creates no successor artifact.

Committed context selections and pull audits are facts. Replay rebuilds the experience projection and validates derivation without calling the selector, reader, renderer, proposer, or provider. Logical time—not wall-clock completion— decides what was prior.

This strict layer preserves causal claims while leaving everyday proposals free to declare no derivation. Experience remains bounded, explicit, and unable to change evaluation, budgets, permissions, or promotion.
